description: Risk Density RRT* plans among obstacles whose positions are uncertain. Each uncertain obstacle is a Gaussian density over its position, combining the obstacle's and the robot's uncertainty. The risk of a motion is the line integral of these densities along it, a first-order approximation of the probability of colliding on the way. A line integral adds up over the edges of a path, so RRT*'s choose-parent and rewiring steps work unchanged with this cost. For a straight motion the integral has a closed form in terms of the error function. A small weight on path length is added to the risk. It keeps paths from making arbitrarily long detours around low-risk regions, and it bounds the informed set, so with a zero weight informed sampling is off. Obstacles with known positions stay with the validity checker. The cost is not a metric, because a straight edge through high risk can cost more than a detour, so RRT*'s asymptotic optimality is not guaranteed; the paper makes the same caveat.

papers.authors: Lorenzo Paiola, Giorgio Grioli, Antonio Bicchi
papers.title: Risk Density RRT*: Planning in the Space of Probability
